To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MRI reliably detects microemboli in coronary arteries and myocardium, and that the presence of coronary microemboli in myocardium delays healing of pre-existing myocardial injury and increases LV remodeling.

(1) MRI is a reliable method to assess regional perfusion, microinfarct and LV function, (2) MRI underestimates the extent of microinfarcts, (3) MRI is a noninvasive technique that can discriminate acute from chronic microembolized tissue and (4) microemboli can migrate out of the vessel and into the extravascular compartment, which may limit the use in occluding hemorrhages and tumors.
MRI is a reliable method to assess microembolization, microinfarct, and LV remodeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method to prevent and reverse coronary embolization.
the development of a novel therapeutic strategy to reverse the deleterious consequences of coronary embolization.
the pathophysiology and clinical significance of coronary microemboli and myocardial microinfarct, and the potential use of microinfarction in treating cardiovascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current knowledge about coronary microemboli, microinfarct and myocardial remodeling is limited, but MRI is a powerful tool for noninvasive assessment of these processes.
MRI is the best available noninvasive method for assessing microinfarct and its effects on LV function.
microembolization is a frequent complication of coronary interventions, and MRI is a valuable tool for noninvasive assessment of microinfarction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microinfarct process is a dynamic process that is dependent on time.
microinfarct can be reliably detected and characterized by MRI and this noninvasive imaging technique may have clinical utility in predicting prognosis of patients with microembolization.
MRI is the best noninvasive tool to assess the extent of microembolization and its effects on the LV and myocardial microvasculature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microinfarct may be a significant contributor to adverse cardiac remodeling and should be considered when assessing the clinical significance of myocardial injury.
MRI is the most sensitive imaging modality to detect coronary embolization and its effects on myocardium.
the presence of coronary microemboli and microinfarcts can be reliably assessed with MRI and that the presence of these microinfarcts is associated with worse LV remodeling.
